main_text.head: Toni ministrorum undecim.
main_text.p: Hæc, inquam, traditur à quibusdam fuisse ratio melodiæ Hebraicæ. Verùm enimuerò nimis incondita, & pro-10inde grauitate, amplitudine, suavitate & sanctitate librorum sacrorum indigna videtur hæc musica.

IV. Musica instrumentalis est, quæ docet canere organis hanc ad rem aptis. Moses Gen.4.v.21. nominibus citharæ & organi (synecdochicè comprehendit15 omnia instrumenta musica; tum ψαλφατα, quæ alijs dicuntur ἔνχορδα & κρουστά, quæ fidibus constant & manu tanguntur, ut citharæ, nablia, tympana: tum πνευματικά sive ἐμπνευστά, quæ digitis ventone mouentur, ut tubæ, buccinæ, tibiæ, & similia organa. Apparatus huiusmodi30 instrumentorum est infinitus. Confer Psalm. 150. cum 1. Chron. 15. vers. 16. & seqq. Dan. 3. v. 10. Passim quoque fit mentio buç inæ: ut Exod.19. Levit. 25. Ios.6. Vsus organorum istorum, ut & totius musicæ, debet esse triplex. Primum35 & præcipuus est, ut Deus celebretur voce & organis. Ac-

page.notes: The musical example has four staves with notes on the staff lines, numbered 1 to 11 in Hebrew cantillation names. Hebrew labels and vowels are copied as legible; vowel points on the small labels are uncertain. The marginal line numbers 10, 15 and 30 are read from the scan; the number 35 and the lines between them are uncertain. The Greek words ψαλφατα, ἔνχορδα, κρουστά and buç are doubtful and marked only in the reading as printed. Spelling of u/v and long s normalised as per the rules.
